name: Magog
title: Japheth's son and ancestor of northern peoples
summary: Magog was the second son of Japheth, who in turn was a son of Noah. He is regarded as an ancestor of peoples in the north, traditionally linked to the Scythians and other groups around the Black Sea and the Caucasus. In prophetic and apocalyptic literature, the name Magog was used symbolically for hostile nations that would rise against God's people in the end times.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the table of nations
keyEvents.description: Magog is listed as the second son of Japheth in the table of nations in Genesis, which describes the origins of the peoples after the flood.

keyEvents.title: Repeated in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Magog's lineage is repeated in 1 Chronicles as part of the genealogical overview from Adam onward.

keyEvents.title: Ezekiel's prophecy about Gog from the land of Magog
keyEvents.description: The prophet Ezekiel prophesies about Gog from the land of Magog, who will attack Israel in the last days but will be crushed by God's power.

keyEvents.title: God's judgment on Gog and Magog
keyEvents.description: Ezekiel describes God's final judgment on Gog and his armies, where fire and sulfur rain down from heaven.

keyEvents.title: Gog and Magog in the Revelation of John
keyEvents.description: In the Revelation of John, Gog and Magog appear as symbolic names for all nations that Satan gathers for the final battle against God's people after the thousand-year reign.
